scope: Resident MTP NextN draft device-chain (task #3 sub-win B): keep the draft chain on-device across depths, remove per-depth host round-trips
hardware: AMD Radeon 8060S / Ryzen AI Max+ 395 (gfx1151, Strix Halo APU, ~256 GB/s LPDDR5X)
change: Each draft depth's top-1 is gathered from a resident FP32 embedding table (exact copy of token_embd_f32) via a new f32 row-gather kernel; top-k accumulates into a device buffer; per-depth device_synchronize + top-k D->H + host-embed H->D collapse to a single drain + readback at chain end; per-depth rope/pos/ctx precomputed and uploaded once. Gated HIPENGINE_RESIDENT_MTP_DRAFT_DEVICE_CHAIN (default off).

correctness.note: Resident embedding rows + gather are an exact copy/select of token_embd_f32, and the rope scratch is zero-padded above rope_w (qk_head_dim=256, rope table 64-wide, kernel reads d/2=128) to match legacy's zeroed self.cos region. Draft tokens are therefore provably identical -> acceptance unchanged by construction.

isolated_propose_chain_B5.command: scratchpad/draft_device_chain_parity.py (20 trials, warmed, device_synchronize per trial)
isolated_propose_chain_B5.bands: non-overlapping p10/p90 -> small but consistent win

memory_cost: resident f32 embedding table = vocab_cap(32768) x hidden(2048) x 4 = 268 MB, lazily allocated only when the device-chain flag is on
conclusion: The device-chain is exact and non-regressive and removes all per-depth host round-trips from the draft, but the draft is GPU-compute-bound (q6_k vocab GEMV + MoE), so the host-sync removal yields only a ~2% isolated sub-window win that is flat at e2e. Consistent with the session's bandwidth/compute-bound finding: host/launch/sync overhead is not the MTP draft bottleneck. Kept behind a default-off flag (concrete blocker for default-on: 268MB resident table not justified by a flat headline); available for rollback/bisection and as the clean resident-draft architecture.
